text:
PIT visits UTA tonight with little separating the teams at five on five, where PIT has taken 55% of the expected goals (a measure of chance quality) and UTA 56%. The gap is at the back end: UTA allows 2.71 expected goals per 60 minutes against PIT's 3.48, while the two create at similar rates (3.52 for UTA, 3.38 for PIT). The model has UTA slightly ahead, 3.32 expected goals to 3.08. Special teams lean UTA's way too, with a power play worth 0.84 expected goals a game against 0.53 for PIT, though UTA takes 4.4 penalties a game and keeps handing out chances.

Neither projected goalie arrives in form. Sebastian Cossa (UTA) starts over Karel Vejmelka, who has 8 of the 9 starts, and sits at -0.75 goals saved above expected (how many goals a goalie stops compared with an average one facing the same shots) across three games, with no data from last season. Arturs Silovs (PIT) is at -0.15 over five games after -12.76 last season in 39 games. UTA is 3-2-0 in its last five with 57% of the expected goals, while PIT is 1-3-1 with 48%. The model likes PIT more than DraftKings does, 46% to win against 38%.

For PIT, Sidney Crosby has a 31% chance to score and 62% to record a point, and Rickard Rakell is listed as due after nine goalless games on 3.0 expected goals (28% to score). Egor Chinakhov could return, day-to-day. For UTA, Nick Schmaltz and Dylan Guenther each sit at 33% to score, and Clayton Keller has a 67% point chance. PIT closing a winless road trip is a storyline the model doesn't price, so it shouldn't be treated as decisive.
